subject: Copywriting
title: Re-Engagement Campaigns
description: A fast breakdown of Re-Engagement Campaigns for builders.

hook.text: 'We miss you' emails have a 12% reactivation rate. Bringing back dead subscribers costs 5x less than acquiring new ones.

buildup.text: Subscribers go dormant after 3-6 months of inactivity. Re-engagement campaigns wake them up before they're lost forever.

discovery.text: The best re-engagement emails acknowledge absence directly: 'It's been a while' feels honest.

twist.text: Adding an unsubscribe nudge—'Want to leave? No hard feelings'—actually reactivates more people.

climax.text: After re-engagement, non-responders should be purged. A clean list with engaged readers outperforms a bloated one.

punchline.text: Wake them or release them. A clean list outperforms a big list.

details.whyItMatters: Acquiring a new subscriber costs 5-7x more than re-engaging an existing one. Re-engagement campaigns protect your investment in list building and often recover surprisingly large segments of inactive subscribers.
takeaways: Re-engaging existing subscribers is 5-7x cheaper than acquiring new ones
Win-back sequences typically use emotion, exclusivity, or preference updates
Unresolvable inactives should be removed to maintain list health

faq.question: When should you send a re-engagement campaign?
faq.answer: Trigger re-engagement after 60-90 days of inactivity (no opens or clicks). Send a 3-email sequence: a friendly 'we miss you' message, a value-forward email showing what they've missed, and a final email asking them to stay or unsubscribe.

faq.question: Should you remove subscribers who don't re-engage?
faq.answer: Yes. Inactive subscribers hurt deliverability — email providers interpret low engagement as a spam signal. After a re-engagement sequence, remove anyone who remains inactive. A smaller, engaged list outperforms a large, unresponsive one.
